pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Embley School | Private school in Romsey, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Embley School | Private school in Romsey, Hampshire
Children progress from Embley as Renaissance individuals, formed into intellectually curious and open-minded young people who seek their personal best in all that they do and are adept at being effective navigators in a sea of change. They are successful, rounded, happy and compassionate young people who don’t think less of themselves, just think of themselves less.
Ours is a school….
Curious
Compassion
Enquirers
for the curious
built on compassion
for the enquirers
Curiosity is encouraged and developed. It informs our children’s enquiry, engages their thinking and makes them adept solution finders.
Curiosity at Embley
Embley Flying Club
This year, we have launched the Embley Flying Club in collaboration with British Young Pilots, offering expert-led tutorials and hands-on training with a flight simulator.
Geography trip to Morocco
Students from Year 8 and 9 had an incredible experience exploring Morocco on a week-long geography tour.
By allowing children to be purposefully uncomfortable, they embrace experiences that provide opportunity to see the world from different perspectives.
Compassion at Embley
With feathers
Did curiosity really kill the cat? Over the course of the year, I interview hundreds of students. Recently I was interviewing a prospective student from Germany. As is often the case we talked about all sorts.
Remembrance Service
Embley students, staff and our wider community came together to honour those who have served through a series of Remembrance events.
To be authentically human is to engage our capacity to reason. Children develop a keen analytical awareness and an ability to discern effectively.
Enquirers at Embley
Art & Design residential to St Ives
Year 9 students enjoyed an inspiring, creativity-packed residential trip to St Ives. Students took part in group activities and had the opportunity to choose from an Art, Photography, 3D Design or Food and Nutrition itinerary.
Wilde
Sometimes in life bad things happen. Sometimes they happen even when we have nothing to do with them, they just happen.
“Our role is to create a generation of young people who will make the world a better place. We shape children to focus on being ‘their’ best. They arrive at a destination that may seem ‘the best’ but are not complacent to settle there. An Embley education brings out a level of achievement in the children that they didn’t know they had.”
As an innovative and forward-looking school, we are purposefully suited to the challenges of the modern world. Our focus is on the formation of young people who don’t just believe in success, they live it authentically.
Beyond their own A*
Our focus is on the formation of authentic and successful young people who can become anything they want to be.
We take children beyond what statistics say they can do. Your child will leave Embley with a promising future ahead of them, a portfolio of strong academic results, a finely tuned emotional and intellectual toolkit.
Embley is an HMC accredited school.
We are a Prep, Senior School and Sixth Form as one; on one breath-taking site and with one shared vision for our children. From the early years of childhood to the final days of Sixth Form, this is a journey we are on together; each member of staff with each child in our care.
A 130 acre classroom
Learning at Embley is not contained by public exam specifications. Alongside a rich academic curriculum sits our programme of over 200 co-curricular experiences, each specifically designed to develop life-long skills that enhance learning and personal development. Set amidst a stunning 130- acre woodland campus, we believe that academic progression and personal wellbeing are enhanced by outdoor adventure, serving others, playing sport and participating in the Arts.
Adventure & Service
From learning about duty and service at our partner school in Ghana, community projects closer to home, our Combined Cadet Force and Duke of Edinburgh programme, to understanding the importance of teamwork and building resilience while sailing on Embley’s fleet of keelboats and trekking the three highest peaks in Scotland, there is nothing better
than seeing the delight on children’s faces when they are allowed to be purposefully uncomfortable and realise what they are capable of.
Explore Adventure & Service
Sport at Embley
We don’t chase silverware, we chase performance because we believe it is the challenge to improve, the resolve to endure and the drive to succeed that inspires the journey rather than the destination. Our focus is on how we get better,
incrementally, humbly recognising how we improve and master our craft. The ‘prize’ is improvement, the silverware just acknowledges it.
The Arts
From being immersed in one of our artist in residence workshops in our purpose-built art studios, to taking to the stage in a whole school Broadway productions to a sell-out audience, or playing alongside acclaimed pianists and composers, we instil a love, appreciation and respect for the
Arts. Embley is alive with the Arts and there’s no better way to experience this than at our annual, rival to Edinburgh, Embley Fringe.
We are Embley
"The overall purpose of Embley is ‘the formation of children’ and clearly education is a part of that. But here, they teach scientists and not students of science – it’s contextualised, meaningful, collaborative, analytical and creative - an intoxicating blend formulated to cultivate inquisitive and thoughtful young people."
“We found the children to be wholesome and curious, with few inhibitions. When we asked them what they liked about the school, one threw her arms in the air and roared 'everything!'"
Read the Good Schools Guide review of our Senior School
"A dynamic, forward-thinking school in a stunning location, where pupils are encouraged to 'find what makes them tick' (whatever that may be) and stretched and challenged to 'be their best selves'."
Read the Good Schools Guide review of our Prep
“Being part of this school has been such a wonderful experience. This is the best decision we’ve made for our children."
“There are so many opportunities at Embley to challenge myself. A sense of adventure is actively encouraged, and I've developed the confidence to step outside my comfort zone and to be more curious which has really helped me with my studies and to understand more about me as an individual.”
“Parents unwavering in their praise for the school's 'focus on the individual', the opportunities beyond the classroom and the 'incredible teachers' who 'nurture their confidence'.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative arts and performing | Embley School, private education in Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Creative arts and performing | Embley School, private education in Hampshire
The Arts
We embrace the Arts in many forms at Embley and our students have the time, space and encouragement to make their creative mark at school. Each year we celebrate our students' work across our Embley Fringe Festival.
It is not our business to turn every student into an artist, but it is our purpose to allow them to celebrate their own inherent creativity. We endeavour to instil a love, appreciation and respect for the Arts in its entirety and the many, transferable skills that students will learn along the way. Whether your child takes part in the Arts at Embley for their personal enjoyment and development or commits to further study for GCSE exams, there is so much to get involved in. To recognise talent and potential in the Arts, we offer Senior School and Sixth Form scholarships.
Discover our Creative & Performing Arts Scholarships
Art
All our students enjoy a creative journey of discovery. We believe that starting with the core skills of drawing and observation allows great ideas to come to fruition.
Students explore a range of media before producing a portfolio of work which can include printmaking, ceramics, photography, painting and textiles. Our airy and open plan Art Studio provides an inspiring space, with personalised ‘pod’ spaces for sixth formers, where students hone their talents as emerging artists. Our 3D Design Workshop is always a hive of activity. With a fully equipped design studio with CAD facilities, and a workshop housing specialist equipment for wood, metal, vacuum foaming, welding, casting and 3D printing, students go an immersive journey from concept to creation. In Year 7 to 9 we teach Food & Nutrition in our custom-built Cookery School. Our artists in residence are always popular for new and emerging artists, engaging students in first-hand experiences, using different media, appreciating a diverse range of artistic styles and the creative career pathways available. Beyond the curriculum, we offer creative courses after school which include dressmaking, photography, workshops focused on specific techniques with an artist in residence, a silver jewellery workshop and chocolate making.
Drama
Our students have a starring role to play at Embley – as a creative and rewarding co-curricular activity as well as being part of the backbone of our academic curriculum.
Hundreds of students get involved in our productions each year, with students taking responsibility for every aspect of our productions under the supervision of our professional team – whether as a performer, director, costume designer, set designer, lighting technician, sound engineer or front-of-house host. The Performing Arts Centre is home to our outstanding Drama Department and is both an extraordinary teaching space for the academic courses we offer as well as our own smaller-scale productions which include musical, contemporary and classical pieces; academic showcases; our Junior Drama Company and Senior Drama Company productions; and House Drama competitions. In the summer months we take advantage of our beautiful school grounds, hosting open air performances of classics such as A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Our annual school productions take centre stage at the Winchester Royal Theatre every summer with recent sell-out shows including Grease, Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, and Bugsy Malone. The professional standard of these shows is simply inspiring and a testament to our students’ talents, enthusiasm, commitment and sheer determination.
Music
Every student at Embley can learn a musical instrument and experience the excitement of performing, and they can learn the skills of modern music production and produce their own collaborations in our purpose-built music studio, which is equipped with the latest studio software.
Be it classic, rock, soul, jazz, punk or hip-hop, there are countless opportunities to perform solo as well as in the school orchestra, bands, choirs and smaller instrumental ensembles. Our musicians get involved in a range of formal and informal recitals with renowned concert pianists and composers, performances, concerts and competitions. Our whole school community comes together for our Carol Service at Romsey Abbey and guests enjoy the delights of our seasonal recitals which showcases our scholars’ work. Taught by specialists, including a diverse range of award-winning peripatetic music tutors, our students are motivated at every level of music making from composition to instrumental and vocal performances. Many of our students go on to achieve external instrumental and vocal accreditations from the Royal School of Music and Trinity College London.
Embley Arts Award
The Embley Arts Award offers a broad range of opportunities and benefits. It is a student-led award which is designed to help grow skills in the performing arts (with a choice of completing the award via Art, Music or Drama).
But in addition to completing a performance, students can build a much broader range of essential skills, including as organisation, leadership, planning and teaching. The Arts Award runs at different grade levels, so students can progress through the programme at Embley. The Gold Arts Award can be used as UCAS points towards a student’s university application. In England, the awarding body is Trinity College London and it is managed in association with Arts Council England. The qualification is regulated by Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation).

pageCache.text:
Senior Sport Programs and Events | Embley School, private education in Romsey, Hampshire
Sport
We are proud of our reputation across many sporting disciplines; from an inter-school to national and international level. Yet we believe the journey to success is as much if not more fulfilling than the winning itself.
Benefits of sport
Along with the mental and physical benefits of sport, we place a strong emphasis on the broader life skills of humility, respect, tolerance, teamwork, resilience and discipline that sets true sports people apart.
From enthusiastic beginners to those pursuing sporting excellence in an established discipline, we celebrate every level of achievement across our community through an inclusive, engaging and creative programme. For potential elite young sports people, we also offer a performance sport scholarship programme which offers a range of benefits.
Discover our Performance Sports Scholarships
Our on-site facilities see students train and compete in our core team sports of rugby, hockey, cricket and netball. Every season, you will find students in weekly squad training after school, with winter cricket training taking place before the start of the school day.
Sailing is a popular sport across the school, with many Senior School and Sixth Form students enjoying our keelboat development and race sailing programmes. We are immensely proud of our keelboat race team who have done incredibly well in recent years at the Round the Island Race, and they have their eyes set on the Fastnet. Athletics, swimming, handball, football, team building activities and fitness training form part of our comprehensive Physical Education programme and these experiences are enhanced with practical workshops with professional athletes such as Alex Danson MBE (Hockey Olympic Gold Medallist) and Serena Guthrie (England Netball). As part of our Senior Games programme for Year 11 to 13 students enjoy a wider range of choice during lessons in addition to our core sports such as rock climbing, paddle boarding, kayaking, golf, archery and tennis.
Elite rugby coaching programme with SW7 Academy
In partnership with SW7 Academy, which is co-founded by Sam Warburton (former international captain of Wales, Cardiff and the British & Irish Lions), students benefit from an elite performance training programme that is usually only available to top rugby academies and professional teams.
They are trained to become better athletes using the unrivalled knowledge and expertise of the SW7 Academy team. The strength and conditioning programme is written specifically for Embley students with moderations for different age groups to aid in their development. Other benefits include pitch conditioning sessions, off feet conditioning and recovery sessions.

Sports Performance Camps | Embley School, private school in Romsey
Sports Performance Camps
This August, Embley launches a new series of Sports Performance Camps, built to accelerate development and raise performance in a focused, professional environment in hockey, netball and rugby. Open to both Embley and non-Embley students, these camps give young athletes the skills, insight and training needed to take their performance to the next level.
Hockey Performance Camp
This three-day non-residential camp combines high-quality coaching with off-pitch athletic development. Training will focus on technical refinement, tactical understanding and decision-making at game intensity, alongside strength and conditioning work. The camp will be led by Embley’s Head of Hockey, Morgan Sturt who is a National League player for Havant HC, a Talent Academy Coach with the South Coast Talent Academy and represented England Colleges as a junior.
Olympic Gold medallist (Rio 2016) and Commonwealth Games medal winner Alex Danson-Bennett MBE will lead a specialist masterclass during the camp. This is a fantastic opportunity for players to learn directly from one of England’s most respected hockey figures, gain valuable insights into the demands of top-level competition, and be motivated to take their game to the next level.
Tuesday 18 to Thursday 20 August
09:00 - 15:00 (lunch not included)
Girls and boys currently in Years 7 to 9 (25/26 academic year)
Netball Performance Camp
Led by Embley's Head of Netball, Zoe Leavers, this performance camp will focus on developing and enhancing players' technical and tactical skills through a series of targeted workshops. The camp is designed for girls who have experience playing netball at school or club level and already have a good understanding of the game. Our aim is to challenge and motivate netballers who are eager to push themselves, grow their confidence, and take their game to the next level.
Miss Leavers has over 30 years of playing experience and during her time at university captained both the England and British universities teams, which she then went on to coach.
Monday 24 and Tuesday 25 August
09:00 - 15:00 (lunch not included)
Current Year 7 to 9 (25/26 academic year)
All girls with a passion for netball
Rugby Performance Camp
Led by Embley's rugby coach, Ben Turner, this non-residential three-day camp will focus on elite skill development, tactical analysis and strength and conditioning. Students will receive position‑specific coaching, allowing them to refine the technical skills most relevant to their role. Training sessions will include a strong emphasis on game‑based scenarios, encouraging players to improve their decision making under pressure. To deepen players’ understanding of the sport, the camp will also feature tactical awareness sessions, a structured strength and conditioning block and a dedicated recovery block. Alongside this, players will receive practical nutrition and hydration advice to help them understand how to fuel their bodies for training, recovery, and competitive play.
Mr Turner has a degree in Coaching and Sports Development and over nine years of experience as Head Coach (U18) at Winchester RFC.
Tuesday 25 to Thursday 27 August
09:00 - 15:00 (lunch not included)
Boys currently in Years 6 to 8 (25/26 academic year)
If you have any questions, please get in touch by email camps@embley.org.uk.

pageCache.text:
Senior Academic | Embley, a private school in Hampshire
Academic
We are ambitious for our students and the highest levels of achievement are regularly met. They are the result of progress.
Your child will be stretched intellectually, to think deeply and critically, by being given time and skills to delve into complex ideas and explore concepts in depth.
We use data about each student’s performance to unlock their potential in a similar way to how an investor will monitor changes in global markets to achieve a return on investment. We scrutinise patterns in a student’s learning across subjects and skill sets to maximise their performance, without ever letting pressure loom heavy over them.
Where a passion to improve runs downhill
We believe that if young people see those at ‘the top’ showing restless passion for self-improvement and service to others then they will learn the very same as they make their ascent.
Great teachers are the heartbeat of Embley. No grandeur of place or sophistication of facility can replace meaningful relationships in a classroom where our teachers spark interest and intrigue. The way each teacher inspires, believes in our students, or just makes them love to learn is truly remarkable. By forging meaningful relationships with every student, having a true understanding of their individual capabilities, and armed with exceptional subject knowledge, our teachers focus their attention where it is needed most, asking good and timely questions that excite, challenge and stretch.
Curriculum - Lower School
The first three years of Senior School provide a broad and stimulating experience of subjects alongside the growth and refinement of learning disciplines that your child will benefit from in their future studies.
Maths is taught according to attainment from Year 8 and English and Science in sets from Year 9 to provide more targeted interventions to students who are preparing for different GCSE exam levels or advanced academic qualifications. All students learn French and Spanish in Years 7 and 8 before selecting one foreign language to study in Year 9. In addition to subjects covering Science and Technology, the Humanities and the Arts, and a timetabled Games afternoon and weekly PE lesson, all students have one lesson a week in our Wellbeing Hub where they explore age-appropriate topics including mental health, money management, careers, discrimination, online safety, sex and relationships, first aid, healthy eating and exercise as part of PSHE lessons.
Upper School
Students study at least nine GCSEs in Years 10 and 11.All take English Language and Literature, Maths and Biology, Chemistry and Physics GCSE. For the remaining choices, any additional combinations of the following subjects can be taken, suiting each student’s academic strengths, interests and aspirations:
Business, Science & Technology
Business Studies, Computer Science, Physical Education
Creative & Performing Arts
Art, Craft & Design, Drama, Food Preparation & Nutrition, Music, Photography, Three-Dimensional Design
Humanities & Languages
French, Geography, History, Politics, Religious Studies, Spanish
In addition to GCSE subjects and a timetabled Games afternoon and weekly PE lesson, all students have one lesson a week in our Wellbeing Hub where they explore age-appropriate topics including post-16 options, university and apprenticeship application processes, careers options and goal setting.
GCSE Options Booklet 2026-28
Beyond academics
Learning at Embley is not contained by public exam specifications, it is designed for the curious and adventurous.
Students embark on academic expeditions across the globe to destinations including Iceland, Washington and Ghana; they compete at Olympiads and global competitions; and immerse themselves in guest lectures and workshops from leading experts and academics. Our 200 option-strong co-curriculum broadens learning, fosters skills, sparks passions and helps lead to successful careers. For our next generation of policy influencers and entrepreneurs, we offer debating, Model United Nations, Politics Society, an Entrepreneurs’ Club and Embley Asset Management which sees students trading live on international markets, introducing them to tangible, complex problem solving and values-based decision making. Future engineers, programmers and scientists, will enjoy our Code Club, Aeronautics Programme, First Lego League Robotics and Green Power Car Challenge, where children are building an electric car and racing on international circuits. And budding strategists will enjoy our Chess, Board Games, Dungeons & Dragons clubs as well as a Poker Club – where students learn the rules, language and maths behind the game.

Learning | Nursery & Pre-School | Embley, private school in Hampshire
NURSERY & PRE-SCHOOL
Learning
Nursery
From the age of two, children blossom in a nurturing and caring environment. As well as literacy and numeracy, each week your child will benefit from dedicated Music, PE and Natural Science lessons with our specialist Prep teachers.
They will start to develop letter and sound recognition in phonics and number recognition in maths, along with their listening and attention skills, understanding of the world, arts and crafts and expressive arts. With a carefully crafted combination of child- and adult-led activities, learning is tailored to a child’s interests and the next stages of their development.
Pre-School
As your child moves into our Pre-School, they are introduced to a more structured environment but still with lots of opportunities for play and discovery centred around their interests.
They will start each day with maths and phonics lessons, working in small groups and learning to work as a team. French is introduced into the curriculum alongside our specialist teaching for Music, PE and Natural Sciences. We help children develop their listening and concentration skills, which includes mindfulness activities such as yoga, threading and dough disco. In the Summer term, the children enjoy a number of transition sessions where they explore the Reception classroom with their new teacher. Our children are led by our Head of Early Years, who is a qualified teacher and all our Nursery & Pre-School staff are qualified Level 3 Early Years practitioners as a minimum.
Early Years Curriculum
Our carefully crafted Early Years curriculum centres around areas for school readiness:
Listening attentively, following instruction, expressing themselves and being aware of others around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Adventure & Service | Senior | Embley, private school in Romsey, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Adventure & Service | Senior | Embley, private school in Romsey, Hampshire
Adventure & Service
Discover yourself at Embley
Our children thrive when their learning is fuelled by a spirit of adventure and new environments packed full of meaningful life lessons. Empowered to cross boundaries and challenge themselves to try something new, your child will discover more about themselves. These experiences and achievements develop a growth mindset and fuel confidence and competencies that they will take back to the classroom as well as forward through life.
Your adventure continues…
From learning about duty and service through community outreach, to understanding how teamwork leads to smooth sailing on Embley’s fleet of keelboats, there is nothing better than seeing the delight on children’s faces when they realise what they are capable of.
All children at Embley are encouraged to be outward looking; understanding that the world does not stop at the end of one’s nose but that it is by enriching the lives of those around them that they will find the greatest happiness. Every child at Embley is encouraged to take part in our 1837 Project.
We are proud to be a strong and sharing community, and our children understand the importance of service at a local and global level. We build links with the causes we are supporting so that the children can better understand the challenges that charities are facing and how their efforts are having a positive impact on society and helping others.
“Pupils display modesty and humbleness about their own attributes, reflecting an egalitarian and compassionate approach to life in keeping with the school aims.”
Each Summer we visit our partner school in rural Ghana, Little Roses, to help with teaching, sports coaching and renovating parts of the school. Embley fundraising has enabled a new water tank to be installed at the school, providing vital clean water to pupils.
Across our Prep and Senior Schools, children lead fundraising initiatives. We have strong links with local care homes, where residents enjoy coming into school to watch our many school performances and we take our classroom into the community.
Exploring adventure and service at Embley
Our children are articulate and confident, with a strong sense of social responsibility. We achieve this by providing an education beyond the classroom that helps them grow intellectually, physically, spiritually and emotionally.
Sailing
Standing tall and just 20 miles from Embley, our fleet of boats are moored at Lymington Harbour. Our sailing programme works closely with the Royal Lymington Yacht Club, with opportunities for the complete beginner to those involved in competitive team racing.
From Year 5, we offer dinghy sailing and Embley is a member of the British School’s Dinghy Racing Association.
Sailing scholarships are also available to students in Years 7, 9 and 12.
Combined Cadet Force
Embley’s CCF provides a platform to develop skills useful in all walks of life. The exhilarating training programme includes fieldcraft, navigation, expedition training, signal and weapons handling qualifications, first aid, archery, and use of our dedicated indoor rifle range.
We have a wonderful relationship with the Historic Army Air Flight (HAAF) charity, also based at Middle Wallop, who have supported our cadets by providing hands-on experience with both fixed wing and rotary aircraft, as well as offering careers advice and guidance within the aeronautical engineering sector.
Duke of Edinburgh at Embley
Valued by universities and employers, the Duke of Edinburgh Award helps students broaden their horizons and develop friendships but perhaps most importantly it helps hone vital skills such as self-discipline, time management, problem solving and communication skills which enhance academic progression.
Being physically and emotionally demanding, expeditions take place in wild, open terrain. They last up to four nights at Silver and Gold level. Taking in some of the most beautiful scenery in the British Isles including the New Forest, Brecon Beacons and Snowdonia, students grow a life-long love for the outdoors and nature.
And so, so much more

Horse Riding

Archery
Calling the next Robin Hood or Katniss Everdeen. From Year 2, your child can choose to learn archery or improve their precision, focus and control by working towards Archery GB badges.
Climbing
This is your child’s chance to climb on ropes, boulder higher grades, learn to be an independent climber, take part in the National Indoor Climbing Awards Scheme and compete against other schools in regular climbing fixtures, which can lead to the National Inter Schools Climbing Championships and rock climbing weekends in the Wye Valley.
Horse riding
Be it learning to walk, trot and canter or compete at higher levels, professional and enthusiastic instructors can help your child develop confidence and riding skills in small groups. This option is available as a co-curricular activity from Year 5.
Scuba diving
For those interested in marine biology and understanding more about our planet under the sea, we offer a PADI Open Water Scuba Diving course with a trained PADI instructor. With scuba gear provided, we practise in the school’s swimming pool before venturing to open water dive sites.
Skiing
Your child can learn to race with our alpine ski racing team and develop their skiing techniques before competing against other schools at a national and European level. We also offer beginner and intermediate ski options for those new to the sport. In addition, there’s the opportunity to join our annual Senior School ski trip to either Canada or Italy.
Ten Tors Challenge
An exciting UK trekking challenge organised by our Outdoor Education team, students learn to become safe, confident and independent in the mountains. Practice weekends take place throughout the year on Dartmoor where your child will learn to wild camp and stay in a local hut before embarking on their main expedition - this year it’s the three highest peaks of Scotland, with our mountain leaders watching over them. As part of the experience, your child can also achieve the Mountain Training Hill Skills award while learning about navigation, group management, ecology, the environment, and flora and fauna.
Community Classroom
Each week, we take our classroom into the community and Senior School students entertain residents of a local care home, lead art and music workshops, share their skills and learn about the lives of the residents.
Volunteering
To support the Duke of Edinburgh volunteering section, your child may wish to help lead one of our Prep School co-curricular activities after school, such as Embley Wild Ones, ballet and sports clubs, as well as Art and Drama activities.

Belonging & Personal Development Senior School | Embley, boarding school in Romsey, Hampshire
Belonging & Personal Development
Belonging
We see first-hand how positive mental health and wellbeing, along with a sense of feeling valued and belonging, fosters a growth mindset and enhances academic attainment. To us, this is the foundation for learning. Belonging at Embley doesn’t simply mean fitting in and being like everyone else, rather being accepted and respected for who we are.
The quality of our relationships - peer-to-peer, student-to-teacher, colleague-to-colleague - underpin this belonging and it is what creates such a special community at Embley. This is how our students grow their sense of wellbeing, develop positive social behaviour, achieve academically, and ultimately make a successful transition into adulthood.
Helping navigate through the teenage years and enabling students to have the understanding and life skills to make informed decisions, is our exceptional Pastoral team who are focused on ensuring the happiness, wellbeing and safety of every child. The team includes our Heads of Year, tutors, Boarding House parents and tutors, matrons and Kate, our school counsellor. PSHE lessons take place in our Wellbeing Hub and our guest speaker programme cover issues such as relationships, consent, mental health and emotional wellbeing, personal values, discrimination, identity, personal finance, careers, online safety, social media, alcohol, vaping and drug education.
For parents, we run workshops offering guidance and ideas about how parents can support their children at home.
We share exclusive access to a specialist online portal with our parents, students and staff. This is a professionally endorsed resource that has been developed by child and adolescent mental health and wellbeing expert, Alicia Drummond. It’s an online platform that has been designed to help parents understand and meet their child’s social and emotional needs as they grow up.
Personal Development & Careers
Our continuous personal development programme helps students better understand themselves, giving them the confidence, self-awareness and knowledge about the endless doors that are open in their futures and empowers them to make informed choices about their lives ahead.
Sitting alongside academic achievement, we help equip students with the knowledge and skills that are highly valued in work and society. While aspirations will be vastly different for every student, our Embley Pupil Profile includes core attributes that every Embley student should aim to be before they leave school
Across the Senior School, students take part in a programme of personal development activities with their tutors and our careers advisor during our dedicated Future Fridays sessions, tutor time and PSHE lessons to nurture and refine these personal attributes. In Years 7 and 8, our focus is on helping students to understand more about themselves and aspirations for when they leave school. In Year 9 these discussions evolve to how these ambitions influence GCSE choices. In Year 10 and 11, students are given the opportunity to participate in career-focused workshops and have a one-to-one conversation with our careers advisor about work experience in Year 10 and 12, A Level choices and higher education options.

University & Career Prep Sixth Form | Embley School, private education in Romsey, Hampshire
University & Career Preparation
The world is changing, the workplace is evolving and different breeds of professionals and professionalism emerging. We assist students with their short-term goals and long-term aspirations as they explore what is possible and the steps to achieving their vision.
To deepen understanding of the professional world that could await them, students hear from industry and university speakers, degree apprenticeship providers and successful business people, from start-ups to multinational firms.
Our Careers Advisor and a dedicated careers resource ensures they make well informed decisions as well as provide support for identifying work experience opportunities, UK and international university choices and applications, as well as everything else that life after Embley holds.
Entry to university has become increasingly competitive in recent years. Our students are guided through every stage of the application process, giving them a competitive advantage by showcasing them at their best – through their academic ambitions, skills and career aspirations. Interview preparation includes an interview practice afternoon for all sixth formers with professionals from a range of professions and industries, and we draw on our teacher’s expertise for subject-specific interview practice ahead of university academic interviews.
Leaver destinations
Reflecting their individual aims and ambitions, our students go on to read a wide range of subjects including Chemical Engineering, Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, English, Music and Sound Recording, Computer Science, Business and Modern Foreign Languages, Law, Biochemistry and History.
A significant number of Embley leavers go on to study at Russell Group universities. An increasing number of students are securing highly competitive degree apprenticeships with Pfizer, IBM and JP Morgan to name a few, or choosing to study at universities across the world.

The Arts at Prep School | Embley School, independent education in Romsey, Hampshire
The Arts
Our creative curriculum is an integral part of every child’s learning experience as they develop fundamental skills of expression, confidence, collaboration and self-discipline. Art, Drama and Music also form part of our co-curriculum, with inspiration often coming from our collabroations with Embley Senior School and Sixth Form students.
Art
Your child will learn about Art from an artist’s perspective in our purpose-built art studio, which is always a hub of activity.
Exploring the use of mixed media, schemes of work include making clay tiles in the style of William Morris, studying perspective to create Lowry-style paintings and exploring pop art and onomatopoeic explosions to create comic book style paintings in the style of Roy Lichtenstein. The children get hands-on in our workshop with Design & Technology tools as they design and complete their design projects, ranging from creating matchstick pyramids to understand structure and height or constructing battery-powered mini kit cars. Beyond the classroom, we offer a whole host of creative co-curricular activities including pottery, arts and crafts, chocolate making, embroidery and creativity club.
Drama
Drama at Embley immerses children into more experiential learning, with improvisations in class around themed topics and texts which complement our English curriculum.
Working with our Director of Drama and specialist Drama teachers, the children have the opportunity to take part in productions such as Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat and Aladdin, our annual Summer Year 6 production and a range of drama workshops with visiting artists. Our co-curricular activities include drama clubs, ballet and dance.
Music
Learning music brings a whole host of important benefits including coordination, pattern recognition, memory skills, confidence and perseverance.
Children from Nursery age have a dedicated music lesson each week, taught by one of our music teachers. Our special relationship with Romsey Abbey is an integral part of school life, with children participating in choral workshops with the Abbey’s Director of Music and performances in the Abbey.
Half of our Prep children elect to learn an instrument with one of our many expert peripatetic music tutors, including wind, string and brass instruments, as well as electric and acoustic guitar, drums, piano and singing. They also enjoy our many music groups including school choirs, orchestra along with recorder, guitar and ukulele group and perform at our Prep Recitals. Children are regularly entered for Associated Board of Music, Trinity and Rock School exams.
Arts Award
Our Embley Arts Award offers a broad range of opportunities and benefits to our children.
This pupil-led award helps children to establish and grow skills in the performing arts (with a choice of completing the award via Art, Music, or Drama). But in addition to completing a performance, they can build a much broader range of essential skills, including organisation, leadership, planning and teaching.
The Arts Award runs at different grade levels, so your child can progress through the programme during their time at Embley.

pageCache.pageTitle: A week of artistic enrichment | Latest News | Embley, private school in Hampshire
pageCache.text:
A week of artistic enrichment | Latest News | Embley, private school in Hampshire
A week of artistic enrichment
As part of Embley’s Enrichment Week, students enjoyed a series of inspiring art workshops led by visiting artists and local crafters.
On Monday, students in Years 7 to 10 took part in a workshop with Winchester-based artist and illustrator Jenny Muncaster. Using acrylic paint on art board, they explored techniques including stencilling and water spraying to build layers of colour, pattern and texture. By the end of the day each student had created a vibrant and unique artwork. Tuesday saw eight students attend a silver clay jewellery workshop where they learned how to transform silver clay into personalised pieces of jewellery. They were fascinated to watch their delicate creations become solid silver during the firing process, producing distinctive pieces that reflected their creativity and individuality. On Wednesday, potter and ceramicist Sue Kelly challenged students to create 3D chickens from clay. Working from hollow clay forms, they added texture and colour using slips to bring their designs to life. The finished pieces will dry over the summer before being fired in Embley’s kiln in the autumn term. On Thursday, students headed to Hengistbury Head in Dorset with sketchbooks and pencils to spend the day drawing and studying the dramatic coastal landscape.

Senior Boarding | Embley, boarding and day school in Hampshire
Welcome home
Boarding at Embley opens a breadth and depth of opportunities for our committed and ambitious students.
As boarders, students can focus on achieving their academic goals while taking full advantage of our facilities and 130 acres of outdoor spaces, enjoying an extensive programme of evening and weekend activities, and building life-long and global friendships – all in a home away from home environment.
Our Boarding team help students grow in all aspects of life as they mature into caring and responsible young adults and develop their independence alongside an understanding, respect and compassion for those around them.
From Year 7, we offer full and weekly boarding for families who live a distance from Embley and flexible boarding options for local children. Embley is a member of the British Boarding Association (BSA), an organisation overseeing boarding schools in 37 countries.
Boarding house
Located at the heart of our school, the Manor House accommodates 70 students in a friendly and bustling boarding house. It’s an impressive and historic building, where boarders enjoy amazing views across the school’s 130-acre estate which turns into their back garden at evenings and weekends and includes tennis courts, woodland and parkland.
Types of boarding
Students live together as one family, seven days a week. After a busy and productive week, boarders enjoy time to relax and reflect, and take part in a weekend programme with the boarding family that is full of cultural, fun and exciting activities and trips – and usually a spot of shopping!
This is perfect for busy families or for students with a long daily commute. Weekly boarders enjoy all the benefits of full boarding and its wrap-around care - a more relaxed start to the day, supervised prep in the evenings, a full range of evening activities and use of the school’s facilities - and return home for weekends to be with their family and local friends.
Flexi boarders have their own bed and dedicated space in the house where they can leave their possessions when not staying overnight. This option helps enormously with those involved in school activities that require an early start or late night - such as sailing commitments, music or drama rehearsals - or to break up the bus journey to and from school.
Evenings
Having completed a full day of study and co-curricular activities, boarders return to the boarding house to change and relax before dinner together. Once supervised prep is complete, they enjoy a range of evening activities which can include baking; board and card games; and arts and crafts.
For the more energetic, there are regular sports activities in our sports hall and gym, students can use the tennis courts and golf course. We welcome day students to spend time with their friends in boarding; inviting them on weekend trips or to our boarders’ birthday parties.
Weekends
We are lucky to be surrounded by the perfect blend of city, coast and country and the school is within easy reach of many places that are steeped in history and academic interest. Saturdays often involve a shopping trip to Southampton or Winchester.
On Sundays, boarders enjoy activities such as swimming, the cinema, trampoline park, horse riding, laser tag, paint balling or paddle boarding. We also arrange trips to places of historical interest such as Stonehenge, Bath or Oxford or to attractions such as Harry Potter World. Embley does not offer exeats.
We are Embley
Welcome to our Boarding Family
Our Heads of Boarding, Mr Johnathan McCredie and Mrs Isabelle McCredie, live in the Manor House. Along with our boarding tutors, dedicated nurses and matron, our boarders are guided and supported academically and pastorally in a happy, safe and secure home-from-home family environment.
Johnathan and Isabelle have worked at a number of international and boarding schools and joined us in 2017 from Bishopstrow College near Warminster where they were joint Heads of Boarding. During the school day at Embley, Johnathan is our Deputy Director of Sport and specialises in rugby and cricket, while Isabelle, is an integral part of the EAL team and holds a CELTA (Certificate in English Language Teaching to Adults) qualification.

Welcome to Embley Senior School
We are a school purposefully suited to the opportunities of the modern world; a world which demands skills and characteristics that stretch beyond excellent qualifications and grades.
Our task is to form incredible and successful young people who can become anything they aspire to be. Students leave Embley as successful, rounded, confident and principled individuals.
We are ambitious for our students and the highest levels of achievement are regularly met. They are the result of progress.
Your child will be stretched intellectually, to think deeply and critically, by being given time and skills to delve into complex ideas and explore concepts in depth.
Ours is a school that values effort as much as achievement, confidence as much as compassion, and pride as much as reflection. Our children don’t just learn a wide canon of knowledge and array of skills, they also learn about how to learn and the subject-specific strategies they can use to enhance their acquisition of knowledge, developing the confidence required to self-regulate and take control of their own progress through Senior School.
Where the fire of ambition burns bright
We believe that the earlier the fire of ambition is lit, the brighter it burns. We take pride in children achieving their academic best. Your child will learn in a community where individuality is celebrated and where a spirit of discovery helps them grow into the best version of themselves. Every one of our teachers is passionate about helping each child realise their potential; their energy and devotion fills every room.
Academic excellence
The first three years of Senior School provide a broad and stimulating experience of subjects alongside the growth and refinement of learning disciplines that lead to successful results at GCSEs, A Levels and beyond.
We use data about each student’s performance to unlock their potential. We scrutinise patterns in a student’s learning across subjects and skill sets to maximise their performance, without ever letting pressure loom heavy over them.
Belonging & Personal Development
The quality of our relationships underpin belonging and it is what creates such a special community at Embley. This is how our students grow their sense of wellbeing, develop positive social behaviour, achieve academically and ultimately make a successful transition into adulthood.
Our continuous personal development programme will help your child better understand themselves and give them the confidence, self-awareness and knowledge about the endless doors that will open in their futures.
Adventure & Service
From learning about duty and service through community outreach, our Combined Cadet Force and Duke of Edinburgh, to understanding how teamwork leads to smooth sailing as part of Embley’s keelboat race team, there are endless experiences to provide a rich balance between academic ambitions and wider aspirational goals.
As part of our global community project, your child could volunteer at our partner school, Little Roses, in remote Ghana or lead workshops with care home residents as part of our classroom in the community work.
The Arts
We embrace the Arts in many forms at Embley and our students have the time, space and encouragement to make their creative mark at school. Each year, we celebrate our students' work in our own version of the Edinburgh event - the Embley Fringe Festival.
To recognise talent and potential in the Arts, we offer Senior School and Sixth Form scholarships.

Careers at Embley
Embley is a wonderful and inspiring place to work. We are proud to be one of the most innovative, ambitious and forward-thinking independent schools in the UK.

We have nearly 200 staff working at Embley across a range of teaching and operational departments, with a strong emphasis on continuing personal development. Training is delivered at Inset days and twilight sessions across the academic year with a programme covering the latest developments in teaching, sharing of best practice and insights from visiting educational experts, including Winchester and Southampton universities and TES.
Staff work collaboratively and observe each other regularly, with professional conversations to support development. Art & Design residential to St Ives | Latest News | Embley School, Hampshire
Art & Design residential to St Ives
Year 9 students enjoyed an inspiring, creativity-packed residential trip to St Ives with activities including Art, Photography, 3D Design or Food and Nutrition on the itinerary.
The trip began at the Eden Project with a macro photography challenge. Students were given subject specific tasks from photographing edible plants to composing images using unique colours, shapes, patterns and textures.
Our Art students spent time at the Tate St Ives, learning about abstract art. They took part in a beach sculpture workshop and a painting 'en plein' workshop where they were challenged to record weather changes and seascapes using watercolours. The students also visited the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden and explored new techniques in a cyanotype photography workshop.
Meanwhile, students interested in Food Preparation & Nutrition had a unique experience at the Porthminster Cafe where they foraged food from the cliff tops and kitchen garden with guidance from the chefs, learnt how to fillet mackerel and enjoyed a delicious meal they had helped to create. They also visited the Bosavern Community Farm, who produce and sell local, sustainable food. Students learnt more about organic food, regenerative agriculture and got hands-on planting trees, farming for potatoes and helping care for the animals. The trip was an exciting, creative and enriching experience for our students.
